text:
Sam: Quick design review request — deployment timeline & rollback flow for rollout page. Trying to decide between a compact history strip vs full vertical timeline. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Priya: I prefer compact by default. Most users glance for the latest status and maybe a single-click rollback. Full timeline can live behind a "Show history" affordance.

Kevin: Backend note: we can page the timeline and return aggregated events for compact view (no extra DB schema). But we need a small API change for canary-group labels if we want human-readable names.

Nora: Agree compact default. Accessibility nits: keyboard focus must move to the rollback confirmation modal, and the timeline updates should announce via aria-live so screen readers know when a canary flips. Also color: current green vs muted green fails 4.5:1 on small text.

Sam: Good call on color. Nora — can you propose a high-contrast palette?

Nora: Yes. Quick mock below (very rough):

```
[Compact timeline] — Latest -> Older 
|● v2.3.1 (canary 10%) — running | ● v2.3.0 — success | ● v2.2.8 — rollback
- Hover expands to show commit, time, author, user-facing note
- Keyboard: arrows left/right move focus between chips, Enter opens details
```

Priya: UX question: where to surface A/B variants vs canaries? Should they share the same timeline items or be separate lanes?

Sam: My gut is separate lanes (stacked compact rows) when variants exist, else a single row. Keeps visual scanning easier.

Kevin: Separate lanes is fine. Implementation detail: lanes map to "deployment target groups" and we already have that concept in the control plane. I can return lane ids + labels.

Taylor: A11y pass offer: I can run a quick axe scan on the mock once Nora updates color. Also suggest adding visible focus ring for keyboard users and an aria-label on the rollback CTA that includes target name (e.g., "Rollback service X to v2.2.8").

Sam: Rollback button placement debate — inline on each timeline item or pinned to top when an item selected? I prefer inline for discoverability, but it must be less accidental.

Priya: Inline but with two-step action: click rollback -> short dropdown to confirm target & optional reason -> final confirm. That reduces accidental clicks and captures context.

Nora: We can make the primary inline CTA a lighter affordance (ghost button) and reserve the destructive red confirm as the final dialog action. Also add a short tooltip on hover explaining the cascade (what services/variants are affected).

design-bot: Figma file updated: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/deploy-rollouts-compact-timeline — frame "Compact + Lanes v2". Please comment on the right side.

Kevin: Dev follow-up: I'll add the API field for lane labels and ensure events include "is_canary" and "variant_id" flags. Expect a PR by EOD tomorrow.

Sam: Decisions for this thread: compact-by-default timeline with expandable details, support for multiple lanes when variants present, inline ghost rollback CTA + 2-step confirmation, keyboard navigation (arrows + Enter), aria-live for updates, update contrast colors (Nora + Taylor to finalize).

Priya: Can we capture the copy for the confirm modal? Draft: "Confirm rollback — This will route traffic from the selected deployment back to the chosen version. Some requests may fail during the change. Confirm to proceed." Any shorter/better wording?

Taylor: Slight tweak: "Confirm rollback — traffic will be re-routed to the chosen version. Some requests may partially fail during the change. Proceed?" Also add link to docs in modal: "Learn more about rollbacks."

Nora: I'll update the mock and push a small accessibility checklist in the figma comments: focus order, contrast, aria labels, live region text.

Sam: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: Nora/Taylor finish a11y and color, Kevin opens API PR, Priya to add copy to the design spec, I'll schedule a quick 20m sync if needed. :thumbsup:
